newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Santos port to begin strike Tuesday - union.
newsitem.headline: Santos port to begin strike Tuesday - union.

text.p: Workers at the key Brazilian port of Santos will go on strike at 0700 local/1000 GMT Tuesday for an indefinite period, the president of the Santos Stevedores Union said.
"A strike has already been called for 0700 tomorrow," Joaquim da Silva told reporters after a meeting of local and national portworkers unions in Sao Paulo.

The strike will include all categories of workers at the port and has been called in protest against the lack of progress in negotiations with steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) over a labor dispute.
Representatives of the National Stevedores Union will meet Tuesday and the strike could spread to national level by Wednesday, said the union's president Abelardo Fernandes.
Twenty-six stevedores have been occupying two vessels at Cosipa's private terminal at Santos for more than 10 days, protesting the company's decision to use its own workers to load and unload ships.

Talks between union representatives and Cosipa officials Friday failed to resolve the deadlock and the stevedores plan to remain on the vessels and peacefully resist any attempt by the Military Police to evacuate them, said Da Silva.
"There is going to be resistance in order to defend their jobs," he said.
Da Silva added that at least 5,000 workers would demonstrate in front of Cosipa's terminal at around 1000 local/1300 GMT Tuesday.
"If (Cosipa) reopens negotiations, the workers could go back to work at any time," he said.
